Whale Safe Fisheries

Confirmed large whale entanglements off the U.S. West Coast increased during the 2014-2018 Large Marine Heatwave event and since that time CDFW has taken numerous steps including development of a Risk Assessment Mitigation Program to address and minimize entanglement risk, with a particular focus on the Dungeness crab fishery For more details on management of the commercial and recreational crab fisheries, visit CDFW’s crab fishery page.

Check this page regularly for updates on CDFW's Whale Safe Fisheries efforts, including recent risk assessments, alternative gear authorization, Conservation Plan development and upcoming changes to regulations to expand CDFW’s efforts to minimize entanglement risk. You may also sign up to receive important updates.

Risk Assessment and Mitigation Program (RAMP)

RAMP was piloted by the California Dungeness Crab Fishing Gear Working Group (Working Group), codified in regulation on November 1, 2020, and amended in regulation effective October 21, 2025. On a regular basis during the Dungeness crab season, CDFW assesses marine life entanglement risk for humpback whales, blue whales, and leatherback sea turtles based on the best available science related to confirmed entanglements and marine life concentrations. When risk is elevated, CDFW will implement management actions based on RAMP Fishing Zones (JPG).

All documents related to the risk assessments, including Available Data under consideration by CDFW and the Working Group, will be posted on this page.

2025-26 Season

June 18, 2026

The Director of CDFW conducted a risk assessment on June 18, 2026, and is continuing the management actions currently in place, including the 15% Gear Reduction and 30-fathom Depth Constraint in Fishing Zones 1-2 for the commercial fishery, and the Crab Trap Prohibition in Fishing Zones 3-5 for the recreational fishery. These management actions will remain in place for the remainder of the statutory season.

December 19, 2025

The Director of CDFW conducted a risk assessment on December 19, 2025, and will open the Fishing Season for the commercial fishery in Fishing Zones 3, 4, and 5 on January 5, 2026, at 12:01am, under a 40% Gear Reduction. A gear setting period for Fishing Zones 3-5 would begin on January 2, 2025, at 8:01am. Fishing Zones 1 and 2 will open with a 15% Gear Reduction once domoic acid and quality testing requirements are met. Currently, Fishing Zones 1 and 2 will be delayed until at least January 15, 2026, pending testing requirements. The Director is also lifting the Crab Trap Prohibition for the recreational fishery in Fishing Zones 1, 3, and 4, effective January 2, 2026, at 8:01am.

October 24, 2025

The Director of CDFW conducted a risk assessment on October 24, 2025, and is implementing a season delay for Fishing Zones 1-6 for the commercial fishery and a crab trap prohibition for the recreational fishery in Fishing Zones 1, 3, and 4. A Fleet Advisory would also be implemented for all Fishing Zones for the recreational fishery. Note that high levels of domoic acid will delay the opening of the recreational fishery from the California/Oregon border south to the Sonoma/Mendocino County line. Recreational take and/or possession of Dungeness crab is prohibited in these closed waters. In the area between the Sonoma/Mendocino County line and Point Reyes, State health agencies are advising the public not to consume crab viscera (guts) to avoid potential domoic acid exposure.

California Dungeness Crab Fishing Gear Working Group

In partnership with the National Marine Fisheries Service and the California Ocean Protection Council, CDFW convened the California Dungeness Crab Fishing Gear Working Group (Working Group) in September 2015. The Working Group is comprised of commercial and recreational fishermen, environmental organization representatives, members of the disentanglement network, and state and federal agencies working to develop and implement innovative approaches to reducing marine life entanglement risk while supporting a thriving Dungeness crab fishery. Archived agendas, meeting summaries, recommendation memos, public comments and other documents related to Working Group operations are available by contacting the Whale Safe Fisheries team.

Commercial Dungeness Crab Conservation Plan

CDFW is seeking an Incidental Take Permit (ITP) for the commercial Dungeness crab fishery under Section 10 of the federal Endangered Species Act. As part of this process, CDFW has developed several drafts of the proposed Conservation Plan (CP) which describes a comprehensive strategy to avoid, monitor, and minimize impacts of humpback whale, blue whale and leatherback sea turtle entanglements in California commercial Dungeness crab fishing gear. The analysis and drafting has been informed by guidance from the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), NMFS's Habitat Conservation Planning Handbook (PDF). CDFW has released three prior CP drafts and has included tribal and public input as appropriate during the drafting process. 

CDFW submitted the most recent draft and ITP application in January 2026. Upon acceptance of the ITP application, NMFS will initiate a public review process under the federal Endangered Species Act and National Environmental Policy Act, which will include opportunities for public comment. CDFW is posting the most recent draft as a courtesy and is not accepting public comments until NMFS notices the draft and initiates the review process. Updates will be provided as they become available on this page. 

  • Draft Conservation Plan for California’s Commercial Dungeness Crab Fishery December 29, 2025 (PDF)

Gear Marking

In many cases, it is difficult to identify the responsible fishery in marine life entanglement events, which results in a high number of unidentified fishery entanglements. To address this issue and improve fishery identification, gear marking requirements are being established for some state fisheries on the West Coast, along with a prohibition on the use of such markings in other fisheries.

California Commercial Dungeness Crab Gear

Line Marking

Line marking requirements for the commercial Dungeness crab fishery as adopted would begin in November 2025. By November 2028, dual-colored purple and black line will be required for all surface line (excluding buoy gangions) and the upper 15 fathoms of vertical lines. The phased approach is detailed below and either manufactured or painted line may be used. Please review the adopted RAMP regulations for specific marking requirements. The flyer (PNG) below also contains more detail

Timeline for line marking
  • 2025 - 2026 Season: All surface gear must be marked
  • 2026 - 2027 Season: Upper 15 fathoms of 25% of deployed gear and all surface lines must be marked
  • 2027 - 2028 Season: Upper 15 fathoms of 50% of deployed gear and all surface lines must be marked
  • 2028 - 2029 Season: Upper 15 fathoms of 100% of deployed gear and all surface lines must be marked

Commercial CA Set Gill Net Line Marking

Starting January 1, 2026, all set gillnets in the state of California must be marked with 1-inch-wide orange nylon straps woven into the headrope. The straps must be at least one foot in length and woven into the headrope at intervals not to exceed every 20 fathoms. Each strap must contain the fisherman’s identification number. Please review the adopted regulations (PDF) for specific marking requirements.

Specific Gear Markings Restricted to Designated Fisheries

Other states are in the process of implementing similar line marking regulations. Starting December 1, 2026, Oregon will require its commercial Dungeness crab fishery to use dual-colored yellow and black lines, while Washington adopted dual-colored red and black lines for its own commercial Dungeness crab fishery. To ensure proper identification, CDFW prohibits all California commercial fisheries from using line markings assigned to another state fishery on the West Coast (Section 181, Title 14, CCR). A line marking prohibition is also in place for recreational crab traps and hoop nets (subsection 29.80(a)(4), Title 14, CCR). You can find more information under this crab recreational FAQ regarding the line marking prohibition. These prohibitions both took effect on January 1, 2026.

Gear Retrieval

There are two sets of regulations allowing for retrieval of lost or abandoned California commercial Dungeness crab traps. Recent changes to regulations have expanded retrieval of lost and abandoned traps after the close of the commercial Dungeness crab season pursuant to Section 132.2(a). Key differences between informal retrieval pursuant to Section 132.2(a) and retrieval as part of the formal program under Section 132.7 are summarized in the table below.

Comparison between retrieving lost or abandoned commercial Dungeness crab gear under Sections 132.2 vs 132.7, Title 14, CCR.
Item Informal Retrieval (Section 132.2(a)) Formal Program (Section 132.7)
Retrieval Permit Required for CDFW No Yes, Trap Gear Retrieval Program (TGRP)
In-Season Trap Recovery Limits Up to 6 traps per trip, unless a waiver is issued Not allowed
Post-Season Trap Recovery Dates July 16 - Oct 31, or as authorized by the Director when implementing RAMP closures 15 days after scheduled season closure (or as authorized by the Director) and until Sept 30
Documentation Requirement Noted on vessel's log On DFW 1059 logbook form-proof of notification
Reporting Requirement Monthly reporting to CDFW Logbooks returned to CDFW at end of retrieval period
Who Owns Retrieved Gear Original Dungeness crab trap owner Retrieval Permittee
Required to Contact Dungeness Crab Permit Holder No Yes, within 7 days
Payment for Returning Retrieved Trap Voluntary, by original Dungeness crab trap owner Yes, by Dungeness crab permit holder or CDFW if all notification and permit conditions are met

Trap Gear Retrieval Program (Section 132.7, Title 14)

The CDFW Trap Gear Retrieval Program allows for retrieval of lost or abandoned commercial Dungeness crab fishing gear following the close of the commercial season. Qualified entities (charitable organizations, sport or commercial fishing associations, local government agencies, and harbor districts) can apply for a Lost or Abandoned Commercial Dungeness Crab Trap Gear Retrieval Permit. Under the program, Retrieval Permittees are entitled to compensation from the responsible Dungeness crab vessel permitholder in exchange for return of the retrieved gear. If compensation is not provided, CDFW issues a payment to the Retrieval Permittee and assesses the Department Trap Fee on a per-trap basis. Dungeness crab vessel permitholders must pay the Department Trap Fee prior to renewing or transferring their permit. Watch a short video overview. Permit Application, Permit Amendment, and Logbook forms are available on CDFW's Commercial Fishing Licenses page.

Commercial Fishermen's Gear Recovery Network

Using the above identified regulatory frameworks, CDFW is also collaborating with Pacific Coast Federation of Fishermen's Associations (PCFFA) to find and retrieve lost commercial Dungeness crab trap gear. If you see lost gear while at sea and are unable to retrieve it, you can report the location of the gear to PCFFA's Commercial Fishermen's Gear Recovery Network using an online form. The online form and more information about the program can be found on the Commercial Fishermen's Gear Recovery Network webpage.

Alternative Gear

CDFW supports development and testing of fishing gear modifications and innovations aimed at reducing the risk of entanglement with Dungeness crab fishing gear. Currently, there are two main pathways for testing and use of innovative/experimental fishing gear: Experimental Fishing Permit (EFP) and Alternative Gear authorization. More information about the EFP program is available on CDFW’s EFP page, as well as from the Fish and Game Commission webpage. More information on Alternative Gear authorization is available below.

The Risk Assessment and Mitigation Program (Section 132.8(i), Title 14, California Code of Regulations) establishes a process for certification of innovative gear types which reduce marine life entanglement risk as Alternative Gear.

Once authorized by the CDFW Director, Alternative Gear can be used between April 1 and the close of the commercial Dungeness crab statutory season in areas otherwise closed to commercial Dungeness crab fishing.

Electronic Monitoring

Beginning in the 2025-26 fishing season, all vessels participating in the fishery must have a satellite or cellular based electronic monitoring system when participating in the California Dungeness crab fishery. The system shall track and record a vessel’s location at a frequency of no less than once a minute during an entire fishing trip when the vessel possesses any Dungeness crab or Dungeness crab trap onboard, when the vessel owner/operator has Dungeness crab gear present or placed in any Fishing Zone, or when the vessel is otherwise participating in the California commercial Dungeness crab fishery. For more information please review the Compliance Guide for the California Commercial Dungeness Crab Fishery Electronic Monitoring Program (PDF) and the RAMP regulations. Contact Whale Safe Fisheries with any additional questions.
